chief_complaint: superficial left wrist laceration and suicidal ideation
hpi_details: 19-year-old university student brought to the emergency department by her roommate after superficially cutting her left wrist last night following a breakup. The wounds have already been cleaned and do not require sutures. She states that she 'just wanted the pain to stop' and now regrets the action, though she admits to still feeling hopeless. She endorses a prior history of cutting herself at age 16. There is no reported substance use. She currently lives in a university dormitory.
ideas: believes that cutting herself was the only way to escape the emotional pain of the breakup
concerns: worries that her hopelessness will never go away and that she might be sent to a psychiatric hospital
expectations: hopes to talk to someone and go back to her dorm today
pmh: History of deliberate self-harm (cutting) at age 16
social_hx: University student living in a dormitory with a roommate. No history of substance use.

boundaries_and_exceptions: If the patient expresses active, ongoing intent to die and cannot contract for safety, involuntary psychiatric admission may be legally and ethically necessary.
While involving a trusted person is standard, confidentiality must be carefully navigated, ensuring the patient consents to sharing information with their roommate or family.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that a 'superficial' physical injury corresponds to a low risk of future suicide.
Relying on a patient's stated 'regret' as absolute proof of safety without completing a thorough, structured risk assessment.
Failing to ask explicitly about the patient's intended outcome (e.g., 'did you want to die?').
Discharging the patient alone without establishing a safety plan or involving a reliable support person.
core_concepts: A comprehensive suicide risk assessment must evaluate current intent, belief in lethality, ongoing ideation, and access to means.
Previous history of deliberate self-harm or suicide attempts is a major risk factor for future attempts and completed suicide.
Management of self-harm in the emergency setting requires both immediate medical care of the injury and ensuring the patient's psychiatric safety.
A collaborative safety plan and involvement of supportive contacts (e.g., roommate, family) are critical components of safe discharge planning if inpatient admission is not indicated.
dangerous_errors: Discharging a patient with ongoing hopelessness and suicidal intent without psychiatric consultation.
Failing to assess the patient's current access to lethal means.
Overlooking the significance of a prior history of deliberate self-harm.
Neglecting to arrange timely follow-up mental health care before the patient leaves the emergency department.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: superficial left wrist laceration and suicidal ideation

Key HPI features: 19F university student brought by roommate after superficially cutting her left wrist last night after a breakup. Says she 'just wanted the pain to stop', now regrets it but still feels hopeless. History of cutting at 16. Wounds already cleaned, not needing sutures.
Relevant background/PMH: History of cutting at 16; no substance use.
management_principles: Conduct a full suicide risk assessment exploring intent, lethality belief, ongoing suicidal ideation, and access to lethal means.
Provide urgent psychiatric referral or consultation prior to discharge from the emergency department.
Develop a collaborative safety plan outlining coping strategies and emergency contacts.
Involve a trusted person (e.g., family member, reliable roommate) in the discharge plan and arrange close follow-up within 24-48 hours.

source_refs.title: American Psychiatric Association (APA) Practice Guideline for the Assessment and Treatment of Patients With Suicidal Behaviors

clinical_knowledge.topic: Suicide risk assessment and management of deliberate self-harm

reference_soap.assessment: Suicide attempt (non-lethal self-injury) in the setting of an acute psychosocial stressor (breakup) and a possible depressive episode. Patient exhibits ongoing moderate risk given her continued hopelessness and history of self-harm, despite expressing regret.
reference_soap.objective: Patient is alert and cooperative but appears tearful and dysphoric. Vitals are stable. Left wrist examination reveals superficial linear abrasions and lacerations that are clean, with no active bleeding, tendon involvement, or neurovascular deficits; sutures are not indicated. Patient maintains eye contact and is communicative but expresses a depressed mood.
reference_soap.plan: Wound care completed; no surgical intervention required. Complete a full suicide risk assessment regarding ongoing ideation, intent, plan, and access to means. Request urgent psychiatric consultation in the emergency department prior to disposition. If deemed safe for discharge by psychiatry, collaboratively develop a safety plan, involve her roommate in the disposition, and arrange urgent outpatient psychiatric follow-up within 1-2 days.
reference_soap.subjective: 19F university student brought in by her roommate after superficially cutting her left wrist last night following a breakup. Patient states she 'just wanted the pain to stop' and currently regrets the action. However, she admits to ongoing feelings of hopelessness. She endorses a prior history of cutting at age 16. Denies current alcohol or illicit substance use.

learning_objectives: Conduct a comprehensive and empathetic suicide risk assessment, explicitly inquiring about intent, lethality, and access to means
Identify historical and acute risk factors for suicide, including prior self-harm, hopelessness, and recent psychosocial stressors
Formulate an appropriate disposition plan that includes psychiatric consultation, collaborative safety planning, and involvement of support systems
Demonstrate appropriate medical evaluation of self-inflicted wounds to determine the need for further intervention

teaching.diagnosis: Suicide attempt (non-lethal self-injury) in the setting of a depressive episode

must_ask.say: When you cut your wrist last night, were you hoping to end your life?
What did you think would happen when you cut your wrist?
Do you have any thoughts of wanting to hurt or kill yourself right now?
Do you have access to any weapons or large amounts of medication at your dormitory?
You mentioned feeling hopeless; can you tell me more about how you see your future right now?
Have you ever attempted suicide in the past, or was cutting at age 16 the only time?
Besides your roommate, do you have any family or friends who can support you during this time?

teaching.one_liner: 19-year-old female presenting with superficial self-inflicted wrist lacerations and feelings of hopelessness following a recent psychosocial stressor.
red_flags: Ongoing suicidal ideation with a specific plan and intent
Access to lethal means (e.g., firearms, stockpiled medications)
Lack of social support or reliable contacts

history.answer: My roommate brought me to the emergency room because I cut my left wrist last night after a terrible breakup.
I don't actively want to die right now, but I still feel completely overwhelmed and hopeless about my life.
I don't have a plan to end my life, and I haven't written a suicide note or said goodbye to anyone.
No, I don't have any weapons, ropes, or stockpiled pills in my room, just my regular school supplies.
I didn't cut myself to end my life; I just felt this unbearable emotional agony and wanted the pain to stop.
I used a small craft blade to make shallow cuts on my left wrist, knowing it wouldn't kill me.
I cut my arms a few times when I was sixteen during exam stress, but I stopped and have never tried to kill myself.
My boyfriend of two years broke up with me yesterday evening out of nowhere, and my whole world felt shattered.
For the past couple of weeks I've been feeling down, crying easily, and having trouble sleeping and focusing on my coursework.
I feel like this deep sadness is never going to go away, and I feel guilty for being such a burden to my roommate.
No, I've never had periods where I felt euphoric, stayed awake for days without feeling tired, or acted recklessly.
No, I have never heard voices talking to me or telling me to harm myself, and I don't have strange beliefs.
I haven't had any alcohol to drink recently, and I do not take sleeping pills or any recreational drugs.
I feel nervous and heartbroken, but I have never felt aggressive or wanted to hurt anyone else.
No, I have never experienced physical, sexual, or emotional abuse, and my dormitory is safe.
I don't suffer from any long-standing pain or serious medical conditions.
No one in my family or among my close friends has ever attempted or died by suicide.
I spoke with a high school counselor a couple of times three years ago, but I have never seen a psychiatrist or taken psychiatric medication.
My roommate has been very supportive and stayed with me, and I know my parents would be heartbroken if anything happened to me.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses like asthma, diabetes, or thyroid disease.
I had my wisdom teeth removed two years ago, but I have never had any other surgeries or hospital stays.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic cigarettes.
I only drink a glass of beer once or twice a month socially, and I didn't drink anything yesterday.
I am a first-year university student, and I live on campus in a dorm room with my roommate.
My mother takes medication for high blood pressure, but there is no family history of depression or psychiatric illness.
I had been in a monogamous relationship with my boyfriend for two years until yesterday, and we always used condoms.
My last period started two weeks ago and was normal, my cycles are regular, and there is no chance I am pregnant.
I felt like cutting my wrist was the only physical way to release the suffocating emotional pain of the breakup.
I am terrified that this hopeless feeling will never leave, and I am scared that you will lock me up in a psychiatric ward.
I really just want to talk to someone about how I feel, make sure my wrist is fine, and go back to my dorm today.

exam.finding: Alert, tearful 19-year-old female maintaining eye contact, appearing visibly distressed and dysphoric but cooperative.
Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Superficial linear lacerations and abrasions on the volar left wrist that are clean, without active bleeding, gaping, or tendon involvement.
Motor strength is 5/5 in wrist flexion, wrist extension, and finger movements bilaterally.
Sensation to light touch and pinprick is fully intact across the median, ulnar, and radial nerve distributions in both hands.
Fully oriented to person, place, and time, with depressed mood and tearful affect, but no evidence of loose associations, delusions, or hallucinations.
